variants.headline: Cyclone hits the colony
variants.sub: The colony has been struck by a cyclone.
variants.body:
A cyclone has hit {colony}. The storm is established, but a particular loss or injury is not. Readers considering {target} should distinguish scrutiny of responsibility from blame for causing a natural event, and should not be asked to accept an invented damage total as part of the report.

A cyclone is not a quantified loss statement. Owners and managers should distinguish the occurrence of a storm from specific effects on premises, output or credit. A prudent assessment can take the event seriously while refusing to attach an invented cost or duration of disruption to its name.

We support {target} against easy blame. A cyclone is not evidence that every hostile claim about stewardship is true, and fair judgment must distinguish the natural event from the conduct being assessed. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
